question: Do the soft bands on v58's face come from the printer setup rather than the model?
hypothesis: The bands are extrusion variation from damp filament or uncompensated vibration; matte PLA shows small flow and speed changes as sheen bands.
prediction: With dried filament and a fresh vibration calibration, the v58 strip's face is even; if the bands stay at the same heights, the cause is elsewhere (slicer or model).
why_this_test: E-001 showed similar bands on both models, so the model change is not the main cause. Baseline conditions were never recorded on any print, so they come first. One v58 strip, 1 hour.

controlled.settings: v55 0.4 process and filament (from the v57 0.4 project)
controlled.filament: Kexcelled K5 PLA M, Light Matte Terracotta (lot C6719062), same spool as E-001

result.owner_words: the last print was much better -- smoother for both fronts -- just a weird artifact on the one end

ai_observations.where: one end of a face, near the tip
ai_observations.likely_cause: seam_position 'back' starts every wall loop at that end tip (G-code: outer walls begin at X128.9 Y201.5, the strip's Y-max end); retraction, wipe and z-hop there leave strings

ai_observations.where: one long edge of the left strip
ai_observations.assessment: thin lip along the cut edge; an artifact of cutting a strip (first layer), not of the tile

result.open: Which baseline steps were done before this print? Are any bands still visible on the faces?
